title: 443. Trigonometry & Periodic Models: Horizontal Phase Shift of a Trigonometric Graph
description: A comprehensive mathematics curriculum progressing from foundational numeracy and core mathematical concepts to algebra, geometry, calculus, linear algebra, probability, statistics, discrete mathematics, optimization, mathematical foundations of AI, advanced pure mathematics, and emerging research methods.

questions.concept: Direction of a shift with subtraction
questions.learningObjective: Identify the horizontal shift produced by subtracting a constant inside the sine.
questions.question: How is the graph of \(y=\sin\left(x-\frac{\pi}{3}\right)\) obtained from the graph of \(y=\sin x\)?

options.label: A
options.text: Shift it \(\frac{\pi}{3}\) units to the left.

options.label: B
options.text: Shift it \(\frac{\pi}{3}\) units to the right.

questions.explanation: Replacing \(x\) by \(x-c\) with \(c>0\) moves a graph \(c\) units to the right. Here the point \((0,0)\) of \(y=\sin x\) moves to \(\left(\frac{\pi}{3},0\right)\), because the new function is zero when \(x-\frac{\pi}{3}=0\).
questions.hint: Find the value of \(x\) that makes the argument of the sine equal to \(0\).

questions.concept: Direction of a shift with addition
questions.learningObjective: Identify the horizontal shift produced by adding a constant inside the cosine.
questions.question: How is the graph of \(y=\cos\left(x+\frac{\pi}{4}\right)\) obtained from the graph of \(y=\cos x\)?

options.label: A
options.text: Shift it \(\frac{\pi}{4}\) units to the right.

options.label: B
options.text: Shift it \(\frac{\pi}{4}\) units to the left.

questions.explanation: Write the argument as \(x-\left(-\frac{\pi}{4}\right)\). The shift is \(-\frac{\pi}{4}\), that is, \(\frac{\pi}{4}\) units to the left. The maximum of \(y=\cos x\) at \(x=0\) moves to \(x=-\frac{\pi}{4}\), where the new argument is \(0\).
questions.hint: Find where the argument of the cosine equals \(0\); that is where the original maximum has moved.

questions.concept: Shift when the argument has a coefficient
questions.learningObjective: Factor the coefficient of the variable to find the phase shift.
questions.question: What is the horizontal shift of \(y=\sin(2x-\pi)\) relative to \(y=\sin 2x\)?
questions.explanation: Factor the coefficient of \(x\): \(\sin(2x-\pi)=\sin\left(2\left(x-\frac{\pi}{2}\right)\right)\). The graph is shifted \(\frac{\pi}{2}\) units to the right. Reading the shift as \(\pi\) forgets to divide by the coefficient \(2\).
questions.hint: Rewrite the argument in the form \(B(x-h)\) before reading the shift.

questions.learningObjective: Find the phase shift when a constant is added and the variable has a coefficient.
questions.question: What is the horizontal shift of \(y=\cos\left(3x+\frac{\pi}{2}\right)\) relative to \(y=\cos 3x\)?
questions.explanation: Factor: \(\cos\left(3x+\frac{\pi}{2}\right)=\cos\left(3\left(x+\frac{\pi}{6}\right)\right)\). The graph is shifted \(\frac{\pi}{6}\) units to the left. The value \(\frac{\pi}{2}\) is the constant before factoring out \(3\).
questions.hint: Divide the added constant by the coefficient of \(x\).

questions.concept: Writing a rule for a shifted sine
questions.learningObjective: Write the rule of a sine graph shifted horizontally by a given amount.
questions.question: The graph of \(y=\sin x\) is shifted \(\frac{\pi}{6}\) units to the right. Which rule describes the new graph?
questions.explanation: A shift of \(h\) units to the right replaces \(x\) by \(x-h\). With \(h=\frac{\pi}{6}\), the rule is \(y=\sin\left(x-\frac{\pi}{6}\right)\). Check: the new graph should cross the axis going upward at \(x=\frac{\pi}{6}\), and \(\sin\left(\frac{\pi}{6}-\frac{\pi}{6}\right)=0\).
questions.hint: A shift to the right subtracts from \(x\); verify with the point that started at the origin.

questions.learningObjective: Locate where a cycle of a shifted sine begins.
questions.question: At which value of \(x\) does the graph of \(y=\sin\left(x-\frac{\pi}{4}\right)\) cross its midline going upward, corresponding to the origin on \(y=\sin x\)?
questions.explanation: The cycle of \(y=\sin u\) starts at \(u=0\). Setting \(x-\frac{\pi}{4}=0\) gives \(x=\frac{\pi}{4}\). At \(x=-\frac{\pi}{4}\) the function equals \(\sin\left(-\frac{\pi}{2}\right)=-1\), a minimum rather than a midline crossing.
questions.hint: Set the argument of the sine equal to \(0\) and solve for \(x\).

questions.concept: Location of a maximum of a shifted cosine
questions.learningObjective: Locate the maximum of a horizontally shifted cosine nearest the origin.
questions.question: At which value of \(x\) nearest \(0\) does \(y=\cos\left(x-\frac{\pi}{3}\right)\) reach its maximum?
questions.explanation: The cosine is largest when its argument is \(0\). Setting \(x-\frac{\pi}{3}=0\) gives \(x=\frac{\pi}{3}\), where \(y=\cos 0=1\). At \(x=-\frac{\pi}{3}\) the value is \(\cos\left(-\frac{2\pi}{3}\right)=-\frac{1}{2}\).
questions.hint: The cosine reaches its maximum when its argument is \(0\).

questions.concept: Phase shift in a full sinusoidal rule
questions.learningObjective: Find the phase shift when amplitude, period, and vertical shift are also present.
questions.question: What is the phase shift of \(y=2\sin(4x-\pi)+1\)?
questions.explanation: Factor the argument: \(4x-\pi=4\left(x-\frac{\pi}{4}\right)\). The phase shift is \(\frac{\pi}{4}\) units to the right. The amplitude \(2\) and the vertical shift \(1\) do not affect the horizontal shift.
questions.hint: Only the argument of the sine matters; rewrite it as \(B(x-h)\).

questions.concept: Phase shift with pi as a coefficient
questions.learningObjective: Find a phase shift when the coefficient of the variable is pi.
questions.question: What is the phase shift of \(y=\sin\left(\pi x-\frac{\pi}{2}\right)\)?
questions.explanation: Factor the coefficient \(\pi\): \(\pi x-\frac{\pi}{2}=\pi\left(x-\frac{1}{2}\right)\). The phase shift is \(\frac{1}{2}\) unit to the right. The value \(\frac{\pi}{2}\) is the constant before dividing by the coefficient \(\pi\).
questions.hint: Divide the constant in the argument by the coefficient of \(x\); the factors of \(\pi\) cancel.

questions.concept: Shifts that leave the graph unchanged
questions.learningObjective: Relate a horizontal shift to the period of the function.
questions.question: Which horizontal shift maps the graph of \(y=\sin x\) exactly onto itself?

options.label: A
options.text: A shift of \(\pi\) units to the right

options.label: B
options.text: A shift of \(2\pi\) units to the right

questions.explanation: Shifting right by \(2\pi\) gives \(y=\sin(x-2\pi)=\sin x\), because \(2\pi\) is the period of the sine. Shifting right by \(\pi\) gives \(y=\sin(x-\pi)=-\sin x\), which is the reflection of the original graph in the \(x\)-axis, not the same graph.
questions.hint: A graph coincides with itself after a shift equal to a whole number of periods.
